articles.originalTitle: Québec museum opens $61m pavilion celebrating renowned artist Jean Paul Riopelle - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Québec Museum Opens New Pavilion Dedicated to Jean Paul Riopelle
articles.excerpt: The Musée National des Beaux-Arts du Québec is opening a $61m pavilion to display works by Canadian Modern artist Jean Paul Riopelle. The three-storey structure echoes the artist's rustic home studio.
articles.content: The Musée National des Beaux-Arts du Québec is opening the Espace Riopelle-Michael Audain Pavilion. The project budget has more than doubled since it was first announced in 2022, reaching $61m, with the Québec government contributing over $40m. The Jean Paul Riopelle Foundation provided at least $20m in funding. Philanthropist Michael Audain, his wife Yoshiko Karasawa, and mining figure Pierre Lassonde have donated more than 60 important works by Riopelle and his contemporaries. Including gifted works, Audain's contribution exceeds $90m. Designed by Montreal-based FABG Architectes, the three-storey pavilion spans more than 5,000 sq. m and features four exhibition spaces. Opening to views of the Plains of Abraham and the Saint Lawrence River, the building's landscape incorporates plants from northern Québec's boreal forest. MNBAQ director Jean-Luc Murray stated that the pavilion will make the artist's work more accessible to the public.

articles.originalTitle: Collectible Art and Design Event PAD London Makes Compelling Case for Luxury Players - WWD
articles.title: PAD London Fair Brings Together Luxury Brands and Collectors
articles.excerpt: Held in Berkeley Square, the PAD London art and design fair continues to serve as a key platform for luxury brands to connect with international collectors.
articles.content: Held every October in London's Berkeley Square, the PAD London art and design fair welcomed new participants this year, including luxury brands such as Yves Salomon and Buccellati. Fair organizers stated that the event attracted younger collectors aged 30 to 45, as well as buyers from the Middle East, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Latin America. Italian jewelry brand Buccellati showcased new designs from its Macri collections and welcomed thousands of visitors to its booth during the event. Yves Salomon Éditions, bringing its renowned ready-to-wear name into the furniture and gallery sector, presented a curated selection of historic and contemporary designs. According to UBS's global collecting report, increases in first-half sales at international auction houses continue to support the recovery in the art and design market.

articles.originalTitle: Chanel Becomes Lead Sponsor of Hong Kong’s M+ Museum in Expanded Three-Year Deal - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Chanel Extends Partnership with Hong Kong M Plus Museum for Three Years
articles.excerpt: French luxury house Chanel has signed on as lead partner of Hong Kong's M+ museum for the next three years.
articles.content: French luxury house Chanel is deepening its relationship with Hong Kong's M+ museum, signing on as lead partner for the next three years. Backing the contemporary visual culture museum in the West Kowloon Cultural District since 2023, the brand is expanding its support beyond film to exhibitions, artist programs, and other projects. The new agreement, announced Wednesday, introduces an initiative called Pioneering Visions to spotlight artists who have shaped contemporary art and visual culture. The first exhibition under the program will be Sarah Sze: Centrifuge, opening at the M+ Focus Gallery in February 2027. Financial terms were not disclosed. M+ director Suhanya Raffel stated the expanded partnership will allow the museum to explore connections between different artistic disciplines. Opened in 2021 and designed by Herzog & de Meuron, the waterfront museum houses over 9,000 works spanning contemporary art, design, architecture, and moving image.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel Paris dispatch: what to see beyond the fair this week - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: New Exhibitions and Venues Open Across Paris Art Week
articles.excerpt: As part of Paris art events, Paris Internationale has opened its doors, while the new contemporary art centre Large has launched on the Île Seguin. Several major exhibitions are welcoming visitors across the city.
articles.content: The twelfth edition of Paris Internationale opened on Quai de Valmy in the Canal Saint-Martin district with 56 galleries and 5 non-profit spaces. In public art presentations, three monumental bronze sculptures by Tracey Emin, presented by White Cube, are displayed at Place du Trocadéro. Kutluğ Ataman's video installation Kuba is exhibited at the Chapelle des Petits-Augustins. At the Musée du Louvre, a joint exhibition featuring works by Kader Attia and Elizabeth Peyton remains on view in the Chapel Room until 14 December. The Fondation Cartier presents works by Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama alongside his installation Things Fall Apart, created from materials retrieved from an abandoned glass factory in Aboso. Additionally, a new contemporary art centre named Large opened on Île Seguin in western Greater Paris. Its inaugural exhibition, Imaginary Engine, places over 50 works from the Renault collection in dialogue with new contemporary commissions.

articles.originalTitle: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Guide - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Opens at Tate Modern
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is hosting an exhibition exploring pictorialism, the first international art photography movement, featuring over 200 rare vintage photographic prints and darkroom experiments.
articles.content: Tate Modern is running the exhibition Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography, which explores pictorialism as the first international art photography movement. The exhibition features over 200 rare vintage photographic prints and unusual experiments with darkroom techniques from around the world. Beginning in the 1880s, pictorialist photographers worked to create images as imaginative, expressive, and technically considered as paintings or drawings by experimenting in darkrooms and studios. The exhibition includes a working darkroom where visitors can learn to make photographic prints using vintage and environmentally friendly techniques on certain days. Featured works highlight figures such as Alvin Langdon Coburn, Bonian Luo, and Soichi Sunami, demonstrating how photographers engaged with painting legacies, human portraits, diverse analogue processes, and modern dance collaborations. The exhibition runs at Tate Modern from 14 October 2026 to 21 February 2027, accompanied by an optional self-guided audio tour.

articles.originalTitle: What do boxing and architecture have in common? For Tadao Ando, it’s a lot - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Tadao Ando Explores Parallels Between Architecture and Boxing in Memoir
articles.excerpt: Eighty-five-year-old architect Tadao Ando shares his life, boxing background, and design philosophy in his first English memoir, Towards Light.
articles.content: Eighty-five-year-old Japanese architect Tadao Ando has detailed the surprising parallels between his brief past as a professional boxer and his renowned architecture career. Having boxed briefly in Osaka during his youth, Ando notes that both disciplines demand a solitary stoic struggle to overcome personal fears and discover hidden strengths. Programmatic and budget constraints in architecture, much like the rigid demands of boxing, force a deep examination of what is truly necessary in design. Raised in working-class postwar Osaka, Ando taught himself architecture from books and completed his first major critical breakthrough, the Row House in Sumiyoshi, in 1976, later receiving the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1995. Translated by Polly Barton and published by Scribe Publications, his new memoir, Towards Light: A Philosophy of Life and Architecture, ventures far beyond technical architectural theory to chronicle personal anecdotes and the author's broader life philosophy. Rather than following a strict chronological structure, Ando wrote freely from his accumulated memories. The book is priced at 25 pounds and aims to leave readers with a renewed sense of hope and inspiration to pursue new paths.

articles.originalTitle: With Few French Design Firms in the U.S., Liaigre Prepares for Growth - WWD
articles.title: French Design Firm Liaigre Prepares for Growth in the United States
articles.excerpt: Liaigre, the French furniture and interior design firm founded by Christian Liaigre, aims to expand its presence in the United States. New CEO Henri Corbin de Mangoux stated that the company will focus on luxury residential and hospitality projects.
articles.content: While the business of French bespoke furniture and interior design remains relatively underdeveloped in the United States, the new chief executive officer of the firm built by the late designer and architect Christian Liaigre plans to change that. Appointed in September, Henri Corbin de Mangoux has been tasked with growing the company's U.S. business and expanding its footprint across luxury residential, hospitality, and branded living projects. Their first priority is to deepen relationships with architects and designers who have long supported the brand, while also reaching new clients such as younger art collectors and successful entrepreneurs. Founded in 1985, the firm is known for bespoke interiors, furniture, and lighting defined by clean lines, refined proportions, and a philosophy of luxurious simplicity. It boasts 23 showrooms worldwide and projects spanning residences, yachts, hotels, and restaurants. Another major priority is hospitality and branded residential work. The company is currently collaborating with Capella Hotels and Resorts on a project housed in a former convent in Florence, expected to open at the end of 2027, and is in discussions with high-end U.S. developers. Furthermore, the firm is exploring new experiential concepts in Miami to reflect the local coastal lifestyle while emphasizing made-to-order French craftsmanship.

articles.originalTitle: sandbag castle casts sustainable concrete alternatives into floating installation in eindhoven - Designboom
articles.title: Floating Installation in Eindhoven Showcases Low-Carbon Concrete Alternatives
articles.excerpt: Visual artist Yvonne Mak has brought together over ten low-carbon concrete alternatives in her floating installation Sandbag Castle, displayed on the Dommel river in Eindhoven, to address the environmental impact of conventional cement.
articles.content: Visual artist Yvonne Mak highlights the environmental impact of conventional cement with her floating installation Sandbag Castle, positioned in the Dommel river beside the Van Abbemuseum Café in Eindhoven. Measuring 5 meters wide and 3 meters high, the structure consists of hundreds of concrete modules resembling stacked sandbags. The design references temporary flood barriers and the widespread reliance on concrete for protective infrastructure. Red warning flags featuring a custom coat of arms with symbols for water, bridges, flora, and hands are positioned at the top of the structure. The physical composition of the work directly incorporates over 10 distinct low-carbon concrete variants, including calcined clay, alternative binders, geopolymer concrete, recycled aggregates, and self-healing concrete formulations. Developed with main partner TBI alongside specialized material and technology contributors, the work demonstrates existing and emerging structural alternatives designed to reduce CO₂ emissions in construction.

articles.originalTitle: David Chipperfield Architects builds concrete gallery around singular artwork in Germany - Dezeen
articles.title: David Chipperfield Architects Builds Single-Artwork Concrete Gallery in Germany
articles.excerpt: A monolithic concrete gallery has been added to the Carmen Würth Forum sculpture garden in Germany to house a large-scale artwork by German painter Anselm Kiefer.
articles.content: The Anselm Kiefer Pavilion has been completed in the sculpture garden of the Carmen Würth Forum museum in Künzelsau, Germany. Designed by the Berlin office of David Chipperfield Architects, the structure was built to exhibit Schwarze Flocken, an 11-by-7.1-metre artwork by German painter Anselm Kiefer, which is named after a poem by Holocaust survivor Paul Celan. Formed to accommodate the massive artwork that previously could not be exhibited in the museum, the cuboid pavilion was constructed using brick and bush-hammered concrete. Its three-layer wall construction comprises concrete, brickwork, and an internal layer of clay plaster, allowing the building to adapt to varying climatic conditions and remain frost-free without active climate control. Inside, the timber roof structure is left exposed, while rooflights introduce natural light to create a tranquil, focused atmosphere that directs attention to the artwork. The entrance features a restrained portico providing shelter and marking the transition between the surrounding landscape and the exhibition space.

articles.originalTitle: Collected - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery to Exhibit Works Acquired for Public Care
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London is bringing together more than 40 works acquired for public care through the Acceptance in Lieu and Cultural Gifts schemes for the first time.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London will host a new exhibition titled Collected from 22 May to 5 September 2027, showcasing a unique selection of rare art works brought from private collections into public care across the UK. Held in the Ground Floor Galleries, the exhibition gathers more than 40 pieces for the first time, featuring paintings and ceramics by Picasso, a glittering cup with a millennium-old history, and an 18th-century goldfish bowl owned by an eccentric collector. Visitors will encounter works by Rembrandt, Renoir and Lucian Freud alongside rare objects acquired through the Art Council’s Acceptance in Lieu and Cultural Gifts schemes. Notable pieces include items accepted by the government in lieu of tax with additional grants from heritage funds. Standard admission operates on a pay-what-you-wish basis, while gallery members enjoy unlimited free entry to all paid exhibitions. The exhibition is supported by Adrian Sassoon and Edmund Burke, offering a comprehensive journey through centuries of artistic treasures and shared cultural heritage.

articles.originalTitle: “Architecture Must Return to Its Essence”: Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu on the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale - ArchDaily
articles.title: Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu to Curate the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
articles.excerpt: Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu have unveiled the curatorial vision for the 20th International Architecture Exhibition, calling for architecture to return to its physical essence and act of making.
articles.content: Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu have been appointed to curate the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, scheduled from May 8 to November 21, 2027, across the Giardini, the Arsenale, and Venice. Titled "Do Architecture – For the Possibility of Coexistence Facing a Real Reality", the exhibition advocates for a return to the physical act of building at a time when the discipline has drifted from lived reality through excessive abstraction, commercialization, and digitalization. Rather than focusing on prospective futures, the curators propose questioning current practices through materials, construction, local knowledge, and direct experience. Building upon the long-standing ethos of Amateur Architecture Studio, which they founded in 1997, the duo emphasizes traditional building techniques, material reuse, and the relationship between place and architecture. The exhibition additionally explores how architecture can unify contrasting conditions such as technology and craftsmanship, as well as urban and rural construction methods.

articles.originalTitle: Frieze London 2026 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze London Art Fair and Contemporary Exhibitions Converge Across the Capital
articles.excerpt: As Frieze art fairs unfold across London, the capital's museums and galleries present a diverse array of new exhibitions and events.
articles.content: Events, exhibitions, and fairs held as part of Frieze art week in London brought together the international art community. Alongside Frieze London and Frieze Masters, various venues across the city hosted distinct exhibitions and projects. The Frieze Masters edition featured increased representation from the Global South, while the 1-54 Contemporary African art fair introduced a new historical strand. A new art fair opened in the former US Embassy building in Mayfair, and the Latin American-focused Paraíso fair staged its inaugural edition. Meanwhile, institutions such as Tate Modern, the Barbican, and the Sir John Soane's Museum contributed to the city's artistic activity with temporary exhibitions. The European Union's new packaging regulations also remained a focal point for galleries and museums navigating sustainability requirements.

articles.originalTitle: Hundreds Protest in Colombia After Far-Right President Removes Works From National Museum - Hyperallergic
articles.title: Removal of Artworks at Colombia's National Museum Sparks Protests
articles.excerpt: The removal of approximately 30 artworks from Colombia's national museum under government orders sparked protests in Bogota, leading to clashes with police outside the venue.
articles.content: Hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside the National Museum in Bogota to protest the removal of artworks addressing political violence and women's rights. Under instructions from President Abelardo De la Espriella, approximately 30 works referencing LGBTQ+ movements, feminist groups, state violence victims, and the 2016 peace accord were withdrawn from display. Stripped gallery walls bore the silhouettes of removed items, while riot police stood ready at the entrance with water cannons and stun grenades. Culture Minister Paola Holguín stated that the museum could not serve as a hub for political indoctrination. Leaders of six modern art museums across the country penned a joint declaration calling for the decision to be reversed. Artists and curators argued that censorship fails to hide the complexity of history and instead makes the targeted subjects more visible. De la Espriella, who assumed office in August, had previously suspended a federal stimulus program for creative workers in September.

articles.originalTitle: too large to exhibit, anselm kiefer's monumental painting gets its own pavilion by david chipperfield - Designboom
articles.title: David Chipperfield-Designed Anselm Kiefer Pavilion Opens in Germany
articles.excerpt: Built in Künzelsau, Germany, a concrete pavilion has opened its doors to house Anselm Kiefer's monumental painting.
articles.content: A freestanding concrete pavilion designed by David Chipperfield Architects has opened in Künzelsau, Germany, to house a monumental painting by German artist Anselm Kiefer. Completed in the sculpture garden of Museum Würth 2, the 140-square-meter structure opened to the public on October 13, 2026, marking the first public exhibition of Schwarze Flocken, a work measuring over eleven meters tall and seven meters wide. The monolithic building features a rough, bush-hammered concrete exterior and an interior with exposed timber beams and skylights that introduce natural daylight. Developed in direct collaboration with Kiefer, the pavilion utilizes an unconventional wall assembly of brickwork and interior clay plaster to maintain frost-free temperatures without active climate control. The space provides visitors with an opportunity to encounter the large-scale painting within an environment tailored specifically to its spatial and material requirements.

articles.originalTitle: Reenvisioning histories of American art: transforming museum practice - Rijksmuseum.nl
articles.title: Reenvisioning Histories of American Art: Transforming Museum Practice
articles.excerpt: As museums face mounting pressure to reckon with histories built on exclusion and exploitation, a new volume highlights scholarship and museum practices aimed at diversifying collections, exhibitions, and staffs.
articles.content: In recent years, museums have faced increasing pressure to reckon with their histories and legacies, many of which depended on exclusion, exploitation, and theft. This institutional self-reflection has emerged alongside a focus on incorporating antiracism and decolonization throughout museum work. Although more museums seek to diversify and make their collections, exhibitions, and staffs inclusive, very little has been published about the actual processes involved in this work. Published by Dartmouth's The Hood Museum of Art in association with the University of Washington Press, a new volume emerged from this ongoing dialogue. The publication highlights new scholarship and museum practices in diversifying collections, exhibitions, and staffs. It discusses new frameworks for how museums develop institutional priorities and aims to interrupt colonial structures in museum curation and teaching art history. Contributions cover topics ranging from collaborative methodologies and Native art acquisitions to Black feminist domesticity and Asian Americana. The volume is available for research use within the Rijksmuseum Research Library.

articles.originalTitle: Anatomy and Astronomy in the National Art Library - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: National Art Library Highlights Early Medical and Astronomical Textbooks
articles.excerpt: The National Art Library at the Victoria and Albert Museum houses rare early textbooks focusing on human anatomy and astronomy.
articles.content: The National Art Library within the Victoria and Albert Museum maintains rare early volumes on human anatomy and astronomy among its collections. Notable items include Andreas Vesalius's volume commonly known as De humani corporis fabrica libri septem, widely regarded as the first accurate anatomical textbook. Working during the Italian Renaissance, the Padua professor collaborated with German artist Jan Steven van Calcar to produce over 250 woodcut illustrations detailing internal human structures. Another scientific volume held in the library is the 1799 second edition of A compendious system of astronomy by Margaret Bryan, a school founder who compiled her lectures on planetary distances and motions for students. The publication refers to Uranus by the historical designation Georgium Sidus, a name utilized for decades following the planet's discovery. These volumes form part of the institution's Clements Collection and are accessible for viewing by appointment within the special collections reading rooms after standard registration.

articles.originalTitle: Designing with Multifunctional Metal Systems - Architectural Record
articles.title: Design Role of Multifunctional Metal Systems in Hunters View Project
articles.excerpt: The multifunctional aluminum sunshades and large-scale wallscreen used in San Francisco's Hunters View residential project demonstrate how envelope design and installation efficiency can be optimized under tight budgets and schedules.
articles.content: In San Francisco's Bayview neighborhood, Hunters View Blocks 14 and 17—a 118-unit LEED Gold affordable housing community designed by David Baker Architects—implemented multifunctional envelope systems. Provided by metal fabricator BŌK Modern, custom anodized aluminum Simple Mount sunshades deliver solar control at windows, while a large-scale wallscreen gives the two-building composition a shared visual identity. Developed by David Baker Architects, the semi-randomized circle-based grid creates dynamic shadows that shift with viewing distance and time of day. Designed with a direct-mount attachment approach, the sunshades eliminated protruding brackets, reduced site mobilizations, and achieved installation costs up to 33 percent lower than conventional systems. Manufactured in California with recycled content, the aluminum systems help reduce cooling loads and support the building's LEED Gold certification. Project stakeholders resolved performance and design intent prior to fabrication through early coordination programs.

articles.originalTitle: Teacher Twilight In-person - Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Special Evening Event for Teachers
articles.excerpt: V&A South Kensington is organizing an exclusive evening event and curator-led exhibition tour for teachers in conjunction with the Constantinople to Istanbul exhibition.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum in London will host an in-person Teacher Twilight event on 29 January 2027, offering educators an exclusive evening of networking and curatorial insights. Taking place at V&A South Kensington from 18.00 to 20.30, the programme provides light refreshments and creative teaching inspiration from the curatorial team behind the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition. Attendees will gain fresh perspectives on 1,600 years of art and design shaped by cultural exchange, alongside updates on upcoming programmes from the V&A Schools and Colleges team. Tickets are priced at £10.00 and include exhibition entry, refreshments, and a complimentary glass of wine. Bookings require school affiliation details and close at 15.30 on the day of the event. V&A members retain free admission to all museum exhibitions as part of their membership benefits.

articles.originalTitle: Meet the collectors | Laurent Dumas - Art Basel
articles.title: New Contemporary Art Center Le Large Opens Near Paris
articles.excerpt: Established by Emerige real estate group CEO Laurent Dumas, Le Large opened its doors in Boulogne-Billancourt, focusing its inaugural exhibition on the industrial history of Île Seguin.
articles.content: Le Large, a new contemporary art center located on the western edge of Greater Paris in Boulogne-Billancourt, has opened to the public. Founded by Laurent Dumas, CEO of the real estate group Emerige, the institution highlights artists living and working in France. The inaugural exhibition, titled 'Moteur Imaginaire', explores the history of Île Seguin, which served as a manufacturing site for the French car company for nearly a century. Curated by Cecilia Alemani, the exhibition runs from October 17, 2026, to March 7, 2027, bringing together around 60 artists including Neïl Beloufa, Bianca Bondi, Théo Mercier, Jean-Luc Moulène, and Laure Prouvost. The presentation aims to showcase the industrial heritage of the former factory site and its connection to labor movements. Laurent Dumas is scheduled to converse with artist Eva Jospin on October 22, 2026, as part of the Art Basel Paris 2026 Conversations program.

articles.originalTitle: Honoring Legendary Designer Yohji Yamamoto and Artist Danh Vo - WWD
articles.title: Yohji Yamamoto and Danh Vo Honored With Isamu Noguchi Award
articles.excerpt: Designer Yohji Yamamoto and artist Danh Vo received the Isamu Noguchi Award at the Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum annual benefit.
articles.content: Fashion designer Yohji Yamamoto and contemporary artist Danh Vo received the Isamu Noguchi Award at the Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum annual benefit. The honorees were recognized for their multidisciplinary practices and artistic integrity. Museum director Amy Hau presented the award, noting Danh Vo's artistic engagement with themes of migration, colonialism, and identity. Yohji Yamamoto, who could not attend, was honored through a special film reflecting on Isamu Noguchi's artistic language bridging East and West. Yamamoto is recognized for challenging conventional ideas of fashion, proportion, and silhouette over a career spanning more than five decades. The annual benefit serves as the museum's primary fundraising event to support its exhibitions, educational programs, and the preservation of Noguchi's archives. The gathering also marked the 75th anniversary of Noguchi's Akari light sculptures.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026: performances, lectures, discussions, roundtables - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Arte 2026 Announces Performance and Panel Programme
articles.excerpt: During the final ten days of the 61st International Art Exhibition at the Arsenale in Venice, a public programme will feature performances, lectures, debates and artist collectives.
articles.content: The Venice Biennale Arte 2026 has announced a public programme of performances, lectures, debates and roundtables for the final ten days of the 61st International Art Exhibition, titled In Minor Keys and curated by Koyo Kouoh. Running from 13 to 22 November at the Arsenale spaces, the schedule features special performances by artists including Laurie Anderson, Ziad Antar, rana elnemr, Natalia Lassalle-Morillo, Sofiá Gallisá Muriente, Clarissa Herbst, Tammy Nguyen, Hagar Ophir, Yo-E Ryou, Dominique Rust, Lerato Shadi and Nathalie Vairac. Alongside these presentations, an Assembly brings together ten artist-led organisations and collectives from various global contexts to share creative practices, discuss pedagogy, and reflect on community and research. The schedule includes panel discussions on resilience and epistemic disobedience, a lecture by Felwine Sarr on mobility and circulation, Tammy Nguyen's maritime-themed performance work Timaeus and the Teacher: Foreword, Hagar Ophir's séance-based presentation, and roundtable sessions paying tribute to historical figures and deceased artists featured in the exhibition. The events accompany the conclusion of the Biennale Arte while establishing new conversations and connections within the international cultural sphere.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Layout for 2026
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries for its 2026 edition, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and a more focused gallery lineup.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition, reaffirming its position as a major commercial moment in the U.S. art market. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3, the fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The redesigned floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features about 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. The new layout organizes the space around four hospitality plazas instead of five, distributing blue-chip galleries throughout the showfloor to improve navigation and sightlines. The event spans multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, welcoming more than thirty first-time participating galleries mostly through its project-based sectors. Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation dedicated to digital art. Public outdoor projects, partner awards, and institutional collaborations will accompany the main exhibition throughout the week.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Moldova Pavilion: HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Moldova Pavilion at Venice Biennale to Host Roundtable on Crisis and Future
articles.excerpt: The Moldova Pavilion in Venice is hosting a roundtable discussion exploring how war and contemporary crises shape the imagination of the future.
articles.content: Organised in collaboration with the Europe Cultural Foundation and the Europe Council for Foreign Relations, a roundtable titled HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis will take place on 16 October 2026 at the Chiesa dei Santi Geremia e Lucia in Venice. The public event, running from 4 pm to 6 pm at the Moldova Pavilion, begins with a tour led by Don Gianmatteo Caputo, priest and architect responsible for the ecclesiastical cultural heritage of the Patriarchate of Venice. Taking Pavel Brăila’s work as a starting point, the discussion expands from Moldova’s geopolitical realities to examine how political thought and cultural practice respond to war and ongoing crises. The panel features former Deputy Prime Minister Nicu Popescu, European Cultural Foundation Director André Wilkens, and art historian Silvia Eiblmayr, with moderation by curator Adelina Luft. The conversation addresses how political and social upheaval calls into question assumptions that previously appeared stable, offering an analytical perspective on contemporary artistic imagination in times of adversity.

articles.originalTitle: ENR 2026 Top 100 Green Design Firms and Contractors: Green Building Market Deepens - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Green Building Market Deepens While Navigating Cost and Policy Challenges
articles.excerpt: While sustainable design and contracting revenues are on the rise, industry stakeholders are grappling with challenges such as federal incentive rollbacks, rising costs, and data gaps.
articles.content: Last year, the revenue of the top 100 green design firms increased by 17.1% to $11.8 billion, while international green design revenue rose 18.3% to $2.15 billion. The revenue of the top 100 green contractors also increased by 5.9% to $101.9 billion. While growth varied across markets, the largest increases were observed in industrial processes, hotels, and health care. However, industry experts point out that the rollback of federal sustainability incentives has created a ripple effect on project costs. Jill Kurtz from Stantec notes that many projects face uncertainties regarding real-world performance, emphasizing that decisions should be grounded in building science and operational data rather than certifications alone. Renée Azerbegi of Mead & Hunt states that shifting policy priorities and reduced incentive programs have generated funding uncertainty. Anica Landreneau from HOK reported that clients are increasingly concerned about grid reliability and energy resilience. Contractors suggest that bringing designers and trade partners together early on is critical in translating sustainability goals into practical decisions.

articles.originalTitle: Ca’ Querini ai Greci - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Historic Ca’ Querini ai Greci Exhibition and Event Space Presented in Venice
articles.excerpt: Located close to San Marco, the historic Ca’ Querini ai Greci building offers dedicated halls and water access for exhibitions, conferences, and cocktails.
articles.content: Situated a short distance from San Marco, the historic Ca’ Querini ai Greci building in Venice features suitable infrastructure for art exhibitions, conferences, and cocktail receptions. The exhibition space on the first floor comprises a central hall of approximately 60 square meters and five large rooms overlooking the Rio dei Greci. The venue provides an exclusive ground-floor entrance and private water access from the canal for loading and unloading artworks. Public transport connections include Actv vaporetto lines stopping at Pietà and San Zaccaria. Available facilities at the Castello address include private water access, bathroom fixtures, lighting, heating, a back terrace, a balcony facing Rio dei Greci, and wi-fi connectivity. Contact details for the location are managed by delegate Antonella Stefani.
